press.title: Escape the press.
press.description: 5 offers a short pass inside. 6 is making a forward run, with a covering defender nearby.

5.label: Keep it with 5
5.why: 5 is behind the approaching defender and offers a short outlet. The ball arrives safely in this scenario, but 5 receives farther from goal, giving the defence time to recover.
5.tradeoff: Useful when keeping the ball matters more than attacking immediately. Next, 5 should look to switch play before pressure arrives.

6.label: Find the run of 6
6.why: 6 runs toward the space outside the covering defender. In this scenario, your early pass reaches 6 before that defender gets across. Waiting longer would make the same pass easier to intercept.
6.tradeoff: Useful when you can pass early and your teammate is already moving. The reward is territory near goal; the risk is a longer pass with less margin for error.

two-on-one.title: Make the defender choose.
two-on-one.description: 6 is running on your right. The defender is between you both, protecting the route to goal.

early.label: Pass early to 6
early.why: 6 receives with room to move. Because you passed before drawing the defender toward you, the defender can shift across and delay the route to goal.
early.tradeoff: An early pass reduces your time on the ball, but may waste the two-on-one advantage. Now 6 must decide whether to take on the defender or return the ball.

carry.label: Carry toward the defender
carry.why: You advance with the ball while 6 continues forward. In this outcome, the defender steps toward you, leaving space on the right. The next action would be a pass to 6 before the defender can recover.
carry.tradeoff: Carrying creates a better passing angle if the defender commits. If they hold their position, reassess; carrying too close can lose the ball. This replay stops at that decision.
